newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JUNE 3.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The victory of the French Left in the weekend's elections created optimism and hopes of relaxed economic policies in Greece although the government was quick to stress that the Greek economy was in no position to let up the pressure to achieve convergence.

--In what is the first significant intervention in the ailing pensions system, the government has submitted an amendment that would change the calculation of lump sum payments for civil servants taking retirement.

--The results of the French elections are fostering hopes for a Maastricht with a social face despite most responses from European capitals stressing that there will be little to no change in the course to European unification.
--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou warmed to the idea of less stringent convergence criteria saying he would "not say no."
--Sixteen pension funds will see reductions of between 20-78 percent in additional pension benefits as of January 1, 1998.
--Greece yesterday saw its first solar-powered school go into operation, inaugurated by Environment Minister Costas Laliotis.
--Former public order minister Stelios Papathemelis's recent comments about knowing the names of those involved with the November 17 terrorist group have caused an outcry.
